sections.h2: What does a Rahway seller need to arrange before closing?
sections.html:
Rahway issues a Certificate of Approval for Continued Occupancy, called a CACO, whenever ownership changes, and the Fire Prevention Bureau separately inspects the house for smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms and an extinguisher. Both items belong on your calendar the day a contract is signed.

Rahway is a compact Union County city of about 3.9 square miles of land, so the city's inspection checklist reaches nearly every sale. About half of its households own: owners live in 51.5 percent of homes. The 2025 estimate is 31,010 residents in 12,257 households. The median owned home is valued at $386,400, owners with a loan pay about $2,702 a month, and median gross rent is $1,845.

The Property Maintenance Division in the Department of Code Enforcement accepts the Application for Certificates of Approval for Continued Occupancy. You check the change of ownership box, list the closing date and give seller and buyer contact details.

Rahway CACO fees, 2025 form
CertificateFee
CACO, residential unit$100 per unit
Temporary CACO, residential unit$100 per unit

Properties with two or more units, and commercial or mixed-use buildings, must first obtain a zoning permit and a Fire Department approval. A temporary CACO is possible once all fire prevention measures are met and the buyer signs an affidavit agreeing to handle the rest.

The city's list of common concerns tells you what to fix in advance:

  • Foundations, roofs, porches and stairs must be sound, with no open cracks or leaks.
  • Stairs with more than four risers need a handrail 30 to 42 inches high.
  • Windows need working glazing and screens on openings used for ventilation.
  • Habitable rooms need two outlets, kitchens need three, and any outlet within six feet of water needs ground fault protection.
  • Cellars and crawl spaces must be free of dampness, and drains must run clear.
  • Peeling paint, loose plaster and decayed wood on interior surfaces must be corrected.

sections.h2: What the Rahway fire inspection looks for
sections.html:
The Fire Prevention Bureau inspects single-family houses when a smoke detector compliance certificate is requested for a sale. A fire safety inspection also accompanies a change in ownership. The city's guidance sets these standards:

  • One smoke alarm on every level, basements included, and none farther than 10 feet from a bedroom door.
  • Battery units must carry sealed 10-year batteries, hard-wired alarms cannot be swapped for battery types, and no alarm may be more than 10 years old.
  • A carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of sleeping areas.
  • One extinguisher rated at least 2A:10BC, no heavier than 10 pounds, mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen and no more than 12 years old.

Replace expired alarms before you book the inspection so a failed visit does not push back closing.

Commuters are the natural audience. Rahway station sits on NJ Transit's North Jersey Coast Line and Northeast Corridor Line, and a typical ride to New York Penn Station takes 38 minutes. A 524-space parking deck stands across from the station, and Newark Liberty International Airport is about a 20-minute drive. Mean commute for local workers is 31.9 minutes.

The downtown has seen new housing, a hotel and shops since the late 1990s, and Merck's headquarters on its Rahway campus anchors local employment. Lead with the train in your listing, and be ready to show buyers that the certificates are in hand.

sections.h2: Flood status near the Rahway River
sections.html: The Rahway River enters from Clark, takes in Robinsons Branch near Elizabeth Avenue and the South Branch near East Hazlewood Avenue, then leaves toward Linden and Woodbridge. If your street is near the water, ask the Building Department for the flood status of your lot, since buyers and insurers will ask for it.

sections.h2: State forms and recording after a Rahway sale
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the Union County Clerk, whose record room holds land transactions from 1857 forward and whose Elizabeth recording office takes documents over the counter on weekdays. The county's online land records search lets you look up records by name, book and page, instrument number or date range.

Gross Income Tax forms depend on who is selling. A New Jersey resident individual, estate or trust signs the GIT/REP-3. A nonresident seller files the GIT/REP-1 at closing, with an estimated payment calculated as the gain times 10.75%, and never less than 2% of the consideration in the deed. The county clerk forwards that payment to the state. An out-of-state heir selling an inherited Rahway house should plan for this withholding. The seller also pays the state realty transfer fee at recording.

sections.h2: A working order of steps for a Rahway sale
sections.html:
Treat the two inspections as a pair. Put the CACO application in with the closing date, the seller's details and the buyer's details. Book the fire inspection in the same week, after replacing any alarms that are past 10 years or running on changeable batteries.

Walk through the house with the city's list: stairs and handrails, outlets, cellar dampness, peeling paint. Fix what you can before the visit. If something cannot be finished, ask whether a temporary CACO fits, which needs fire prevention measures complete and a buyer affidavit.

For a two-family or mixed-use building, begin with the zoning permit and Fire Department approval, because the CACO cannot go forward without them. A pre-1978 rental also gets dust wipes, so allow for that visit. Have your attorney confirm the deed and GIT forms before the closing appointment, and keep the certificates handy for the buyer's lender.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale a good fit in Rahway?
sections.html:
It can be when repairs would take longer than your closing window allows. An as-is buyer takes on the repair list, and a temporary CACO can let the sale proceed once fire prevention items are met and the buyer signs the affidavit.

Ask each buyer who files the CACO application, who pays the $100 fee, and who handles reinspection. Judge offers by what you net after payoff, repairs and fees. If the house has tenants, ask how the buyer will handle them, and remember that a rental built before 1978 carries a higher fee and dust wipes.

faqs.q: Does Rahway require an inspection before a house sale?
faqs.a: Yes. A CACO is needed when ownership changes, and the Fire Prevention Bureau inspects single-family houses when a smoke detector compliance certificate is requested for a sale. Apply early so both inspections fit before closing.

faqs.q: How much is a Rahway CACO for a residential sale?
faqs.a: The 2025 application lists $100 per residential unit for a CACO and $100 per unit for a temporary CACO. A rental built before 1978 costs $125 per unit and receives dust wipes during inspection.

faqs.q: Can I close in Rahway with repairs still unfinished?
faqs.a: Possibly. A temporary CACO is available when all fire prevention measures are completed and the buyer endorses an affidavit agreeing to address the remaining inspection items. Properties with two or more units need zoning and Fire Department approval first.

faqs.q: What must a nonresident Rahway seller pay at closing?
faqs.a: A nonresident files the GIT/REP-1 and makes an estimated Gross Income Tax payment equal to the gain times 10.75%, subject to a 2% of consideration minimum. The payment goes through the county clerk with the deed.

faqs.q: Where can I look up Rahway property records?
faqs.a: The Union County Clerk's online land records search lets you search by name, book and page, instrument number or date range, and the record room in Elizabeth holds land transactions from 1857 to the present.
